survey_design.weight_fields_interpretation: The ICILS Teacher Panel is an extension of ICILS 2018 and uses sampling weights to support population-representative estimation. For the teacher-level database, the final panel estimation weight is labeled TOTWGTT, constructed as the product of the ICILS 2018 baseline weight and a panel attrition adjustment factor. Panel attrition was handled by predicting participation (PART) using weighted logistic regression with baseline observables from ICILS 2018, trimming extreme predicted probabilities, and then using inverse predicted participation probabilities to form the adjustment. Variance estimation uses Jackknife Repeated Replication with 75 replicate weights, with standard errors computed from replicate estimates. The report presents descriptive and regression-based change analyses (e.g., difference-in-differences) rather than ML prediction; therefore, weights and replicate weights are used for statistical inference consistent with the ILSA complex sampling design.

data.handling_not_reported_explanation: This report does not analyze cognitive achievement outcomes with ICILS/PISA-style plausible values. The dependent variables are teacher/principal questionnaire responses and derived scales (e.g., ICT use, ICT self-efficacy, views, and ICT learning-environment perceptions) and the main analyses compare percentages/gaps across 2018 and 2020. Missing data handling is not specified as a single PV-related procedure; instead, the report describes that missing values were converted to central tendency measures when fitting the participation models used to construct panel weights, but it does not provide a general missing-data strategy for all substantive analyses.

sample_details.sample_filtering_criteria: The baseline for the panel consists of the schools and teachers who participated in ICILS 2018 in Denmark, Finland, and Uruguay. The Teacher Panel in 2020 collected teacher questionnaire data from teachers eligible for ICILS 2018 (excluding those who left the profession) and from schools still operating in 2020. For the teacher questionnaire, the reference class was adapted to the grade most similar to grade 8 in 2020 using a country-specific grade hierarchy; teachers who did not teach the target grade used the nearest grade according to the hierarchy. For derived indicators of students’ ICT use and teaching practices, responses were treated as missing when teachers indicated they did not use the practice with the reference class or when students did not engage in the specified activity, and those cases were excluded from the corresponding percentage calculations. Panel data cleaning removed cases where respondents were contacted in 2020 but were not part of the ICILS 2018 panel sample (i.e., they did not respond in 2018), so the final panel sample reflects longitudinal participation.

data.outcome_summary: This ICILS Teacher Panel report uses longitudinal teacher questionnaire data collected in 2020 with ICILS 2018 as baseline to study whether inequality of educational opportunity changed between low- and high-SES schools (defined via a school-level national SES index aggregated from student-level parental occupation/education and books at home). Across Denmark, Finland, and Uruguay, the report finds no clear systematic widening or narrowing of SES gaps from 2018 to 2020; most opportunity gaps remain small in both years. However, several isolated changes appear, including significant SES-gap changes in Finland for teacher preparation time and opportunities to develop ICT expertise, and significant SES-gap increases in Finland and Uruguay for students’ ICT use in explaining and discussing ideas with other students. The analyses are descriptive/regression-based (e.g., difference-in-differences) rather than machine-learning prediction, and inference accounts for the complex ILSA sampling design using TOTWGTT/TOTWGTC weights and Jackknife Repeated Replication replicate weights. The report also cautions that panel response rates are relatively low, which may limit generalizability.
data.null_fields_interpretation: This extraction targets an official assessment framework, user guide, or technical manual without an empirical ML study. Sample sizes, ML algorithms, and predictive findings are intentionally null or empty per schema rules for non-empirical IEA/OECD documentation.
